messages:
maria: quick sync — acme pilot just confirmed SSO requirement for their compliance review. they want it in v1, not v2. customer is blocking go/no-go. need a decision in next 24h.

devon: do we have a clear scope for "light SSO" vs full sso? engineering effort varies a lot.

samir: can we quantify risk/effort? rough numbers: light SSO (OIDC redirect + config UI) ~ 1 sprint + testing. full SSO (role mapping, enterprise provisioning, SCIM) ~ 3 sprints + infra.

lee: +1 samir. also regression surface for auth flows — need extra e2e and canary time. if we push, release window moves.

olivia: support notes — Acme says compliance means they can't ship without SSO in v1. It's a contracted pilot; legal asked.

maria: ok. proposal: ship light SSO in v1 (core auth + simple UI) and scope SCIM/role-mgmt to v1.1 behind a canary. to make room, cut analytics dashboard and the usage-insights export from v1.

devon: analytics dashboard is big. cutting it buys ~3 dev-weeks. that matches SSO light work, but introduces product risk for launch narrative.

lee: alternative: keep dashboard but cut multi-tenant admin UI and defer advanced reports. that also frees ~2-3 weeks. smaller customer-facing impact?

olivia: customers that saw the preview care more about tenancy admin than analytics. i'd prefer dashboard cut over admin UI cut.

samir: tech note: implementing light SSO first means we should avoid toggles that complicate session handling. simpler implementation reduces regressions.

maria: decision lean: light SSO in v1, SCIM/roles to v2, cut analytics dashboard from v1. track it as a formal scope swap. any strong objections?

devon: no objection, but need runway for canary and rollback. request: add a fallback routing policy so if SSO causes failures we can flip customers back to legacy auth quickly.

lee: will add canary plan. estimate 3 days for canary infra + docs.

release-bot: scheduled-release-window: 2026-04-07 to 2026-04-09. Current branch protection enforces freeze 72h before.

maria: timeline implication: if we accept this cut, we still meet the scheduled release, but freeze shifts testing earlier. implies devs need to land by EOD Tue.

olivia: i'll update pilot comms to set expectation: "SSO lightweight in v1; full provisioning in next patch".

samir: action: samir + devon to draft minimal SSO design doc today. lee to write canary rollback steps. maria to confirm cut in roadmap doc and notify stakeholders. olivia to update customer messaging.

maria: thanks — if everyone can ack in thread i will mark the scope change. :thumbsup: 

devon: ack

samir: ack

lee: ack — will post canary steps by EOD

olivia: ack — preparing comms draft

maria: leaving this thread open for one last check. if no new objections, i'll update the milestone tracker and cutlist by 9pm PT.

devon: tiny ask: include a token-level latency SLO note for auth path in the tracker so optimize can see it.

maria: done — added SLO note to tracker (action: maria).

release-bot: milestone-updated: release-window retained, scope-change recorded in release notes PR #4521 (draft).
